speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a generalized nonpruritic rash and a recent history of high fever and seizure. To begin our assessment, could you tell me exactly when your fever started and how long the seizure lasted?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola). The clinical triad of high fever, a generalized nonpruritic rash starting on the trunk and spreading outward, and a recent seizure (likely febrile or hypoxic) in an up-to-date infant is highly characteristic of measles, often complicated by pneumonia or encephalitis.
